title: The Uncommon Initiative of High Talent
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article distinguishes ordinary initiative, solving problems without being asked, from the rarer kind exhibited by top talent: identifying gaps invisible to others and independently building solutions without seeking permission first. The author identifies four ingredients behind this uncommon initiative: curiosity, courage, proactive purpose, and creative ideation. Crucially, the highest performers don't wait to gauge whether leadership will be receptive before investing their effort; they act first and present their work afterward, undeterred by the risk of rejection. The piece closes by urging leaders to watch for this trait and, ideally, to model it themselves.
points: Ordinary initiative solves visible problems; uncommon initiative identifies gaps others don't even see
The highest-talent team members build solutions independently, without waiting for permission or approval
Four ingredients define uncommon initiative: curiosity, courage, proactive purpose, and creative ideation
Top performers act despite the risk of rejection, rather than waiting to gauge leadership's receptiveness first
quotes: Speak to experienced leaders and ask them to describe the most talented team members they have ever worked with, and they will tell you that those colleagues took uncommon initiative.
The most talented team members ignore traditional hierarchy and, without thought for approval or acceptance, work to identify the needs, gaps, and opportunities that are not obvious to others.
Uncommon initiative typically shares four critical ingredients: one part curiosity and openness, one part courage and boldness, one part proactive purpose, and one part creative ideation.
The highest talent doesn’t think that way or care about acceptance or deployment. When they see a big gap or opportunity, they seize the initiative.
They know that real opportunity never knocks. They open the door anyway.
